description: Sh!t-Faced Shakespeare: Romeo & Juliet “Call me but love, and I’ll be new baptized.” There is no love lost between the Capulet and Montague families and everyone in Verona knows it. Certainly the only way to mend centuries of bad blood is by having two forlorn teenagers from opposite households fall in love with each other, right? Nothing that a swig (or two) of the finest spirits can’t fix! Featuring Shakespeare’s most famous feuding family, cousins without a cause, and so many faux deaths it makes daytime TV look good. Our drinker has been known to contribute profanity, and the occasional bare butt-cheek. If any of this puts you off, maybe another show is more your speed. *Warning: But also, we do have sword fights, loud sounds, and flashing lights if those affect your person.* About Shit-faced Shakespeare®: An entirely serious Shakespeare play, with an entirely shit-faced cast member. The original, award winning, international smash-hit direct from London’s West End to an American theater near you! Founded in 2010 in the UK and first arriving on US shores back in 2015. Shit-faced Shakespeare® has delighted audiences all over the States with their highfalutin cocktail of traditional Elizabethan theater and balls-to-the-wall drunken shenanigans. Accept no poor relations, pale imitations or paltry recreations, see the authentic Shit-faced Shakespeare® show which started it all. Featuring a revolving cast of Boston’s finest actors, the choicest cuts of Shakespearian classics and more inebriated antics than you can violently shake a cod piece at. Shit-faced Shakespeare® is the unique theatrical experience that has left audiences roaring in the aisles the world over. description: Classes teach Broadway style tap and focus on repetitive technique to encourage muscle memory and the confidence to create clear sounds. Inclusion is a priority so that all students feel welcome. Classes are “drop-in”, meaning you may join any week and there’s no “semester” commitment. Past steps are always reviewed with the introduction of 1 or 2 new steps or combos each class. Similar to a yoga class, students work at their own individual levels and build up skill at their own pace. Beginners will feel comfortable regardless of when they join. Tap dancing began as an answer to the horrors of colonial enslavement…with no musical instruments, Irish and West African slaves turned to their own feet to create rhythms and percussion while pulling movement and technique from traditional tribal and cultural dances. Sounds were initially made with wooden soles, then pennies and bottle caps, finally becoming the modern metal plates screwed to the ball and heel of the shoes. These dances made their way to minstrel and vaudeville shows, eventually transforming into the broadway and rhythm style tap dancing we know today. description: Classes will begin with a focus on technique, followed by choreography incorporating the mantón de Manila. This class is best suited for students with prior experience working with a mantón and will culminate in a performance in the spring. Cost: $35 Single Class | $224 Entire Series (7 classes) REGISTER HERE What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Flamenco is a form of song, dance, and instrumental (mostly guitar) music commonly associated with the Andalusian Roma (Gypsies) of southern Spain. (There, the Roma people are called Gitanos.) The roots of flamenco, though somewhat mysterious, seem to lie in the Roma migration from Rajasthan (in northwest India) to Spain between the 9th and 14th centuries. These migrants brought with them musical instruments, such as tambourines, bells, and wooden castanets, and an extensive repertoire of songs and dances. In Spain they encountered the rich cultures of the Sephardic Jews and the Moors. Their centuries-long cultural intermingling produced the unique art form known as flamenco. (https://www.britannica.com/art/flamenco) What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I have been dancing and performing flamenco professionally for over 30 years. Throughout my career, I was also a member of three local flamenco companies: Ramon de los Reyes Spanish Dance Theatre, Omayra Amaya Flamenco Sin Limites and my own company, Flamenco Dance Project. I have studied both here and in Spain, and continue my studies (to keep current with the dance) at various workshops both here and abroad. Finish this statement: I am passionate about teaching this style because… it fills my soul, and I want to impart that to my students. I make it a point of really studying the different elements of the dance, especially el cante (singing) to teach my students the importance of the relationship between the dance and the singing. description: A guided improvisational movement practice that engages somatic awareness to facilitate personal growth, emotional well-being, and collective healing. Through verbal instructions, participants are invited to explore, in their own bodies way – a variety of movement patterns, physical inquiries, and focal points. It is a journey where you might sweat (though you are always in control of your rhythm and pace).This class allows you to engage with the wisdom of your own body, to take you on a journey. description: This class is fun and challenging! We warm up, practice basic movements, and then assemble them into a sequence. Capoeira Angola developed in Brazil from a variety of African roots. N’golo from Angola, rhythms from Congo, and acrobatics from Guinea combined to form a martial art disguised as a dance and played like a game. All these elements plus a deliberate sense of fun result in a vigorous workout for the body and mind! What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? Mestre Deraldo: I started training Capoeira when I was 14 years old and just turned 64. I saw Capoeira played on the streets, and was curious to know more. I fell in love with the music, history, and movements of the style. I graduated as a Mestre in 1984 and moved to Boston in 1986. I was the first to teach Capoeira in New England. Mestre Joao Pequenho certified me as a teacher of Capoeira Angola in 1991. Contra Mestre Calango: I moved to Boston in 2000 to continue training with Mestre Deraldo. Since then, I traveled with him to universities and events around the world to assist in demonstrating and teaching of the beautiful art of Capoeira Angola. I graduated as a Contra Mestre in 2017. The term “house” was derived from The Warehouse, a Chicago club where the music was often played. Though the essence of the dance is purely freestyle, popular steps performed in NYC dance clubs were eventually recognized as “house dance foundation.” Members of NYC’s Dance Fusion were the first to teach house dance, which contributed greatly to house becoming a worldwide phenomenon. title: Dickens' " A Christmas Carol"
description: Step back in time and experience a unique blend of history, music, and theatrical tradition in the historic Press Room at the Omni Parker House, the very hotel where Dickens first gave voice to his beloved tale, A Christmas Carol. Veteran actor Johnny Kinsman performs an elaborate reading of Dickens’ cherished story featuring the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge, his spirited encounters with the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Yet to Come, and the heartwarming transformation that follows. Vocalist Ann Moss and multi-instrumentalist Justin Ouellet enrich the story with a luminous musical soundscape, interweaving timeless carol tunes with foley sound effects to create an immersive and magical listening experience. title: Joe Hunt Group
description: $15 admission / Start 8:30pm / Doors 8pm / Seated Show Modern jazz played by Boston's best jazz musicians. Joe Hunt is a jazz drummer, educator, author, and historian. In the early 1960s, Joe Hunt performed and recorded alongside the late NEC Distinguished Artist-in-Residence Emeritus George Russell, with releases on Decca and Riverside. Hunt joined The Stan Getz Quartet in 1964, recording several releases on Verve, then was a member of the Bill Evans Trio from 1966-1967. The remainder of the 1960s found Hunt performing or recording with several other jazz luminaries including Chet Baker, Eric Dolphy, Dizzy Gillespie, Dexter Gordon, Charles Mingus, Bob Brookmeyer, and the late Herb Pomeroy. In the 1970s and 1980s, Hunt was a member of The National Jazz Ensemble, led jazz groups with John Scofield, Mike Stern, and Santi Debriano, and toured with quartets of Red Rodney and Hal McKusick. The 1990s, and beyond, have included membership in The Smithsonian Jazz Masters Orchestra, with former NEC president Gunther Schuller, performances with Kenny Burrell, Joe Lavano, Joanne Brackeen, and Tal Farlow, as well as recordings with the Bert Seager Quintet, and also, Trio. Hunt is the author of the 1994 book 52nd Street Beat, which is a historical look at jazz drummer greats from 1945 to 1965. The Joe Hunt quartet features a modern jazz ensemble music played by top local pros: Mark Pinto - alto saxophone, formerly years with the Buddy Rich band John Lockwood – bass, formerly with Joe Henderson, Lee Konitz, current Fringe member Yuka Hamano Hunt – piano, voice, arranger Joe Hunt – drums, formerly with George Russell, Stan Getz, Jim Hall, Dexter Gordon, and Bill Evans We pay tribute to a special composer or performer at most performances. Recent shows have included: Burt Bacharach, Ahmad Jamal, Bill Evans, and Gigi Gryce. Future shows will include the music of Paul and Carla Bley, and arranger, Johnny Mandel. - Continuing of the 3rd Sunday of Every Month

Tap dancing began as an answer to the horrors of colonial enslavement…with no musical instruments, Irish and West African slaves turned to their own feet to create rhythms and percussion while pulling movement and technique from traditional tribal and cultural dances. Sounds were initially made with wooden soles, then pennies and bottle caps, finally becoming the modern metal plates screwed to the ball and heel of the shoes. These dances made their way to minstrel and vaudeville shows, eventually transforming into the broadway and rhythm style tap dancing we know today. title: Jerry Bergonzi Quartet
description: $15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Plamen Karadonev, Piano Sean Farias, Bass Special Guest , Trumpet A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination, Jerry Bergonzi has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. — By Scott Yanow, AllMusic Continuing Every Monday at 8:30pm Lineup subject to change

title: Intermediate/Advanced Ballet with Dean Vollick
description: Class begins with a thorough set of exercises at the barre that last from 30 to 45 minutes. Centre practice follows, and may consist of a battement tendu exercise, a battement jeté exercise, a grand battement exercise, small and/or large adage, stationary turns, traveling turns, and petite and grand allegro enchaînement (small and big jumps). Classes are structured so that the dancer warms up their feet, legs, hips and upper body gradually. As class progresses there are more changes of weight and eventually, sudden changes of direction. Live music is provided by a pianist, that ranges from classical pieces to selections from ballet repertoire to improvisational contemporary music. Cost: $20 Single Class | $15.00 barre | 5-class package $90.00 *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. Please register in studio with the class assistant Accepted Payments: Cash, Check, Venmo What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Ballet originated in the Italian Renaissance courts around 1500 as large balls or spectacles that were performed by members of the royal court. The French king, Louis XIV, created the first academy and the positions, steps, and movements of the ballet were collected and codified. The spectacles began to be performed by artists that were trained in the academy, originally as part of an opera, and later as ballets that told a story through music, mime, and dance. Linear Salsa is a hybrid dance that comes from Mambo (a Cuban style that was popularized in the 1950’s NYC Palladium). NY Mambo is a marriage of footwork and partner-work from Cuba (Aftro-Cuban movements, Cuban Son) and the U.S. (Jazz, Swing). Salsa is a marketing term popularized in the 1970’s to commodify all Latin music and dance to a U.S. audience. Circular Salsa primarily comes from the Cuban dance Casino, which itself originates from Cuban Son. Salsa is by nature transformational, multinational, and multigenerational, embodying the shared heritage of Latin music. title: In-Person Bellydance
description: In this class, you’ll explore earthy Egyptian, Turkish, and American style movements, dynamic combinations, and expressive choreography blending tradition and innovation. Experience the power of fiery hip-locks and shimmies, and the fluid beauty of serpentine undulations. Drawing from decades of study with master teachers and over thirty years of performance experience, Johara offers expert guidance in a supportive, inspiring environment—honoring the depth of this ancient art while inviting each student to discover their own unique style within it. Instructions: Wear comfortable dance or workout clothing that allows you to move freely. Classes are danced barefoot or in dance shoes. Students will be encouraged to acquire a veil and finger cymbals (zsagaat/ills). Cash preferred, or Venmo Drop-ins always welcome! What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? The more authentic name for this dance form is raqs sharqi (“dance of the East”), and its roots lie in the Middle and Near East, primarily in Egypt and Turkey. This dance form was introduced to the United States and Europe at the turn of the 20th century, but it was not widely performed or taught until the 1950s and 1960s, when the belly dance craze swept across the U.S. The American cabaret style of belly dance is rooted in the legacy passed down by notable American teachers and performers, who blended Middle Eastern influences with their own innovations and movement styles drawn from diverse dance backgrounds. title: Glimmer ~ Somatic Improvisation + Embodied Choreography
description: Glimmer invites you to move with present moment awareness, connect to your internal experience of what you sense and feel, and bring it your own self expression to the collective experience of moving in community. Every Glimmer gathering weaves somatic improvisation and guided choreography from a wide range of classic, contemporary and conscious dance/movement modalities. Your Glimmer guides (Julianne + Audrey) provide a theme that informs both the somatic improvisation (the research) and the choreography (the collective container). You can count on irresistible playlists from a mix of music genres designed to engage the senses, emotions and imagination, while sensory-based prompts invite us to tune into our bodies to access the creative intelligence that flows within. Simple, guided choreography serves as a container for integrating your movement impulses, your a-ha moments, your “glimmers!” Cost: $20 single class | $195 for 11-class series – 9/12 – 11/28 (no class 10/3) *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? Yu-Ling Hu was trained in four styles of Spanish Dance and she was a former dancer of Ensemble Español Spanish Dance Theater from 2007 to 2016. Yu-Ling founded Yuling Spanish Dance in 2017 and she has been offering Flamenco classes and performances. title: ‘Froca Fitness – African and Caribbean Dance Fitness
description: Students can expect a high-energy, joyful African and Caribbean dance-fitness experience that combines easy-to-follow choreography, rhythmic movement, cardio, and culturally inspired dance styles. The class is designed for all levels, from beginners to experienced dancers, with modifications and repetition that allow everyone to participate at their own pace. Sylver’s teaching philosophy is rooted in creating a welcoming, judgment-free environment where students can connect with the music, move freely, build confidence, and have fun while getting a great workout. African and Caribbean dance traditions are rooted in the diverse cultures of countries such as Madagascar, Senegal, Ghana, Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti, Jamaica, Trinidad & Tobago, and Cuba, among many others. The movement and rhythms represented in ’Froca Fitness draw inspiration from forms such as Malagasy dance, Sabar, Azonto, Kizomba, Coupé-Décalé, Ndombolo, Afrobeats, Dancehall, Soca, Kompa, and traditional Haitian rhythms, reflecting generations of African and Caribbean cultural expression, resilience, and exchange. ’Froca Fitness honors this legacy by bringing these influences into a contemporary, high-energy dance-fitness experience that celebrates the diversity and global impact of Afro-diasporic movement and music. title: Beginner and Intermediate Tap for All Levels
description: Classes teach Broadway style tap and focus on repetitive technique to encourage muscle memory and the confidence to create clear sounds. Inclusion is a priority so that all students feel welcome. Classes are “drop-in”, meaning you may join any week and there’s no “semester” commitment. Past steps are always reviewed with the introduction of 1 or 2 new steps or combos each class. Similar to a yoga class, students work at their own individual levels and build up skill at their own pace. Beginners will feel comfortable regardless of when they join. Cost: $20 for 1 hour | $25 for 90 minutes *NEW* The Dance Complex requires ALL visitors to have a Membership, Guest Pass, or $5 Day Pass to access the building. Registration: Email or text Christina Harrington to register: charrington9901@gmail.com | (617) 852-6240 Pre-registration is encouraged but not required. Drop-ins are welcome. Accepted Payments: Cash, Venmo (@christina-harrington-7) What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Tap dancing began as an answer to the horrors of colonial enslavement…with no musical instruments, Irish and West African slaves turned to their own feet to create rhythms and percussion while pulling movement and technique from traditional tribal and cultural dances. Sounds were initially made with wooden soles, then pennies and bottle caps, finally becoming the modern metal plates screwed to the ball and heel of the shoes. These dances made their way to minstrel and vaudeville shows, eventually transforming into the broadway and rhythm style tap dancing we know today. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? Christina Harrington joined The Dance Complex as a Teaching Artist in May 2012. As a child she studied tap, jazz, and ballet at the Paula Coffey Dance Center in East Bridgewater, MA from 1987-1995 where tap was always her favorite. description: The main goal of our class is to have fun and feel the joy of movement and expression. We also strive to build technical competence and an appreciation for Brazilian culture through music and dance. We start with a warm-up, work on technique and styling, and often learn a short combo. Samba is a rhythm and a dance that exudes equal parts beauty, spirituality, and resistance. Borne in Brazil from enslaved Africans, samba has spread to the mainstream and is now one of the country’s most famous exports. Samba is constantly evolving in all of its forms; currently there are many popular samba sub-genres, including pagode, samba rock, bossa nova, etc. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I was the first to teach Capoeira in New England. Mestre Joao Pequenho certified me as a teacher of Capoeira Angola in 1991. Contra Mestre Calango: I moved to Boston in 2000 to continue training with Mestre Deraldo. Since then, I traveled with him to universities and events around the world to assist in demonstrating and teaching of the beautiful art of Capoeira Angola. I graduated as a Contra Mestre in 2017. title: Chris Smither
description: Having distilled his own signature sound of blues and folk for over 50 years, Chris Smither is truly an American original. A profound songwriter, Chris continues to draw deeply from the blues, American folk music, modern poets and philosophers. From his early days as the New Orleans transplant in the Boston folk scene, through his wilderness years, to his reemergence in the 1990s as one of America’s most distinctive acoustic performers, Chris Smither continues to hone his distinctive sound. He has always traveled his own road and stayed true to his musical vision. He may be best known for writing “Love You Like A Man” which Bonnie Raitt and, more recently, jazz great Diana Krall have covered. His music has been covered by numerous artists and featured in soundtrack albums, independent film, television, and commercials. Reviewers continue to praise his dazzling guitar work, gravelly voice and songwriting. The New York Times: “With a weary, well-traveled voice and a serenely intricate finger-picking style, Mr. Smither turns the blues into songs that accept hard-won lessons and try to make peace with fate.”

Shen Yun opens a portal to a civilization of enchanting beauty and enlightening wisdom, leaving millions around the world in awe. Find out why! Shen Yun Performing Arts is a New York-based nonprofit organization. Its mission is to revive 5,000 years of traditional Chinese culture. Shen Yun cannot be seen in China today. THE STUNNING BEAUTY AND POSITIVE ENERGY leave audiences uplifted and inspired. The message of truth and hope resonates with audiences everywhere. “This is the best I have ever seen. It was so uplifting. It spoke to everything that is good in this world.” —Glen Duncan, Grammy Award-winning musician “It makes you dream of a heavenly world. It’s something that really restores you, regenerates you.” —Filippa Giordano, famous Italian-Mexican Singer “I am so blessed to watch it. I felt a very strong, beautiful energy.” —Paige McNamara, dancer “Shen Yun brought something most needed in this world—hope: hope for a better world, hope for a better future, hope for a better life.” —Jesse Miranda, producer “Shen Yun is a transformative experience for body, soul, heart, and mind. This is the wisdom of all the ancient lineages.” —Douglas Beechwood, producer “Absolutely the greatest of the great! The words to describe it might be ‘divine,’ ‘reborn,’ and ‘hope.’ You have to see it to believe it.” —Christine Walevska, master cellist Sat, Dec 26 7:00pm - 9:15pm Sun, Dec 27 1:30pm - 3:45pm Mon, Dec 28 1:30pm - 3:45pm General admission: $107

title: Beginner and Intermediate Tap for All Levels
description: Classes teach Broadway style tap and focus on repetitive technique to encourage muscle memory and the confidence to create clear sounds. Inclusion is a priority so that all students feel welcome. Classes are “drop-in”, meaning you may join any week and there’s no “semester” commitment. Past steps are always reviewed with the introduction of 1 or 2 new steps or combos each class. Similar to a yoga class, students work at their own individual levels and build up skill at their own pace. Beginners will feel comfortable regardless of when they join. Accepted Payments: Cash, Venmo (@christina-harrington-7) What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Tap dancing began as an answer to the horrors of colonial enslavement…with no musical instruments, Irish and West African slaves turned to their own feet to create rhythms and percussion while pulling movement and technique from traditional tribal and cultural dances. Sounds were initially made with wooden soles, then pennies and bottle caps, finally becoming the modern metal plates screwed to the ball and heel of the shoes. These dances made their way to minstrel and vaudeville shows, eventually transforming into the broadway and rhythm style tap dancing we know today. As a child she studied tap, jazz, and ballet at the Paula Coffey Dance Center in East Bridgewater, MA from 1987-1995 where tap was always her favorite. title: Jerry Bergonzi Quartet
description: $15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Plamen Karadonev, Piano Sean Farias, Bass Special Guest , Trumpet A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination, Jerry Bergonzi has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. — By Scott Yanow, AllMusic Continuing Every Monday at 8:30pm Lineup subject to change

Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums, graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. title: Intermediate/Advanced Ballet with Dean Vollick
description: Class begins with a thorough set of exercises at the barre that last from 30 to 45 minutes. Centre practice follows, and may consist of a battement tendu exercise, a battement jeté exercise, a grand battement exercise, small and/or large adage, stationary turns, traveling turns, and petite and grand allegro enchaînement (small and big jumps). Classes are structured so that the dancer warms up their feet, legs, hips and upper body gradually. As class progresses there are more changes of weight and eventually, sudden changes of direction. Live music is provided by a pianist, that ranges from classical pieces to selections from ballet repertoire to improvisational contemporary music. Please register in studio with the class assistant Accepted Payments: Cash, Check, Venmo What is the legacy of the genre/form/style you are teaching? Ballet originated in the Italian Renaissance courts around 1500 as large balls or spectacles that were performed by members of the royal court. The French king, Louis XIV, created the first academy and the positions, steps, and movements of the ballet were collected and codified. The spectacles began to be performed by artists that were trained in the academy, originally as part of an opera, and later as ballets that told a story through music, mime, and dance. Over the centuries ballet has influenced folk dance styles of many (mainly European) nations and, more recently, has been influenced by folk, modern, and contemporary forms of dance from all countries. What background, training, and or relationship do you have with this style/technique/class subject? I had a professional dance career that spanned more than twenty years and included company work in both ballet and contemporary companies as well as dancing, choreographing, and teaching as a freelance artist.

Linear Salsa is a hybrid dance that comes from Mambo (a Cuban style that was popularized in the 1950’s NYC Palladium). NY Mambo is a marriage of footwork and partner-work from Cuba (Aftro-Cuban movements, Cuban Son) and the U.S. (Jazz, Swing). Salsa is a marketing term popularized in the 1970’s to commodify all Latin music and dance to a U.S. audience. Circular Salsa primarily comes from the Cuban dance Casino, which itself originates from Cuban Son. Salsa is by nature transformational, multinational, and multigenerational, embodying the shared heritage of Latin music. description: In this class, you’ll explore earthy Egyptian, Turkish, and American style movements, dynamic combinations, and expressive choreography blending tradition and innovation. The more authentic name for this dance form is raqs sharqi (“dance of the East”), and its roots lie in the Middle and Near East, primarily in Egypt and Turkey. This dance form was introduced to the United States and Europe at the turn of the 20th century, but it was not widely performed or taught until the 1950s and 1960s, when the belly dance craze swept across the U.S. The American cabaret style of belly dance is rooted in the legacy passed down by notable American teachers and performers, who blended Middle Eastern influences with their own innovations and movement styles drawn from diverse dance backgrounds. Tap is an American dance form in which rhythms are audibly tapped out on the floor. It has origins in slavery and the percussive dances of West African Juba dance and Irish step dancing. It developed through minstrel shows and vaudeville in the late 19th century and emerged along with jazz in the 20th century into the art form we know today. Sela teaches adult beginner and intermediate tap classes at the Dance Complex, and made her Dance Complex choreographic debut at the 2018 Spring Teaching Artists and Student Concert with students from the intermediate tap class.

title: New Year’s Celebration Concert
description: Ring in the New Year with Boston Baroque at our annual celebration of music and new beginnings! Last year, Marc Minkowski made an unforgettable Boston Baroque debut with Handel’s Water Music . The evening culminated in an unexpected encore: an arrangement of ABBA’s “Gimme! Gimme! Gimme!” that brought Sanders Theatre to its feet. Minkowski now returns as Boston Baroque’s Music Director to lead a program devoted entirely to Beethoven. Over nearly a decade, Beethoven repeatedly revised Fidelio , his only opera, composing four overtures as the work evolved. This program brings together the three known as the Leonore overtures , offering a rare opportunity to hear them in a single concert. Also featured are the Romance No. 2 for violin and orchestra and the Choral Fantasy for fortepiano, vocal soloists, chorus, and orchestra. The program will also include a few musical surprises. In 2027, orchestras and audiences around the world will mark the 200th anniversary of Beethoven’s death. Join Boston Baroque in welcoming this commemorative year with a celebration of his revolutionary legacy and a toast to the year ahead. Dates/Times Thursday, December 31, 2026 | 7:30 PM Friday, January 01, 2027 | 3:00 PM Location Harvard’s Sanders Theatre | 45 Quincy St, Cambridge, MA 02138 Ticket Prices $25 – $125 | 10% off for subscriptions

These dances made their way to minstrel and vaudeville shows, eventually transforming into the broadway and rhythm style tap dancing we know today. I was the first to teach Capoeira in New England. Mestre Joao Pequenho certified me as a teacher of Capoeira Angola in 1991. Contra Mestre Calango: I moved to Boston in 2000 to continue training with Mestre Deraldo. description: Classes teach Broadway style tap and focus on repetitive technique to encourage muscle memory and the confidence to create clear sounds. Inclusion is a priority so that all students feel welcome. Classes are “drop-in”, meaning you may join any week and there’s no “semester” commitment. Tap dancing began as an answer to the horrors of colonial enslavement…with no musical instruments, Irish and West African slaves turned to their own feet to create rhythms and percussion while pulling movement and technique from traditional tribal and cultural dances. Sounds were initially made with wooden soles, then pennies and bottle caps, finally becoming the modern metal plates screwed to the ball and heel of the shoes. These dances made their way to minstrel and vaudeville shows, eventually transforming into the broadway and rhythm style tap dancing we know today. title: Jerry Bergonzi Quartet
description: $15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Plamen Karadonev, Piano Sean Farias, Bass Special Guest , Trumpet A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination, Jerry Bergonzi has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. — By Scott Yanow, AllMusic Continuing Every Monday at 8:30pm Lineup subject to change

title: The Fringe
description: $15 @ the door / $10 students / 10pm doors / 10:30 start / seated The Fringe originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist George Garzone , bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums, graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. title: Physical Comedy Technique: Acting & Clowning Shake Hands
description: 8 Week Clown Class with Sheriden Thomas What makes a good clown can make a better actor—and what makes a good actor can make a better clown. Come play with the tools that make comedy work. We’ll put timing, progression, dynamics, status, and physical storytelling center stage, along with a playful glossary of techniques and sayings gathered over decades of studying, performing, directing, and teaching acting and physical theatre. The goal is not simply to understand why something is funny, but to discover how to make it happen—and happen again. We’ll work with a shared vocabulary for recognizing, creating, sharpening, and repeating comedy onstage. Come play. Come discover what your silly self already knows about being funny. The series will culminate in a showing of the work. INSTRUCTOR BIO: Over several decades, Sheriden has acted under Actor’s Equity Contracts in the nation’s regional theatres. Starting in the 70’s, playing ingénues for the Guthrie Theatre in Minneapolis to Boston’s Moonbox Productions, garnering a Boston Critics Award for Kimberly in Kimberly Akimbo . Recently, in film, she played two Grandmas. One in Tiffany Paulson’s About Fate and another in Eric Aronson’s Any Day Now . (Now available on Prime) Sheriden has directed and taught acting at Cornell and Southern Methodist Universities. Since arriving in Boston, she directed plays and readings for Another Country, Queer Soup Productions, and Boston Playwrights’ Theatre. As Senior Lecturer Emerita, at Tufts University, she taught a variety of acting courses including Advanced Acting Lab, Shakespeare, Mask, and Physical Comedy. She directed a dozen plays, concluding with an edited video of Jeffrey Hatcher’s delightfully, silly adaptation of The Government Inspector . title: Barbed Wire
description: January 15–17, 2027, 8pm (Fri + Sat) and 2pm (Sun). Each year we celebrate MLK – the person and the weekend – with a performance focused on the legacy of Black America from Civil Rights to today. This year we bring to the stage Barbed Wire , a new work presented for its first full production on our stage. Barbed Wire by African American playwright Mary E. McCullough and Japanese American playwright Rosanna Yamagiwa Alfaro, traces the unlikely friendship that develops during World War II in a Japanese American incarceration camp between Johnny, a Black soldier stationed there, and Sam, an internee. The two young men meet at a barbed wire fence, a literal and symbolic divide, and their shifting relationship evolves over time as they navigate identity, duty, and survival. The play asks what it means to belong, to serve, and to remain human in systems designed to divide us. It’s difficult to lead a normal life when your country has deemed you less than human and the enemy. Alfaro’s father, Asian American, was head of the U.S. Army Japanese Language School at the University of Michigan during the War . McCullough’s father, African American, was drafted into the Army and served in the Pacific during World War II. Venue Information: The Multicultural Arts Center is located at 41 Second Street in Cambridge, MA. Please enter at the ground floor entrance and visit the Box Office on your right as you enter. Once you check in, you will head upstairs to the theater. There is an elevator and staircase for access to the theater. Seating is general admission. Box Office will open an hour before the show starts, so you are welcome to arrive early. Feel free to visit our gallery before the show begins. Getting There: The Multicultural Arts Center is located just a few blocks from the Green line Lechmere MBTA Station. The East Cambridge Parking Garage is entered off Spring Street, between First & Second Streets, one block away from us, and open 24/7.

description: Sh!t-Faced Shakespeare: Romeo & Juliet “Call me but love, and I’ll be new baptized.” There is no love lost between the Capulet and Montague families and everyone in Verona knows it. Certainly the only way to mend centuries of bad blood is by having two forlorn teenagers from opposite households fall in love with each other, right? Nothing that a swig (or two) of the finest spirits can’t fix! Featuring Shakespeare’s most famous feuding family, cousins without a cause, and so many faux deaths it makes daytime TV look good. Content Curious? Our shows feature murder, treason, war, violence (personal, sexual, and national), suicide, regicide, incest, and blasphemy- and that is just the Shakespeare! Our drinker has been known to contribute profanity, and the occasional bare butt-cheek. If any of this puts you off, maybe another show is more your speed. *Warning: But also, we do have sword fights, loud sounds, and flashing lights if those affect your person.* About Shit-faced Shakespeare®: An entirely serious Shakespeare play, with an entirely shit-faced cast member. The original, award winning, international smash-hit direct from London’s West End to an American theater near you! Founded in 2010 in the UK and first arriving on US shores back in 2015. Shit-faced Shakespeare® has delighted audiences all over the States with their highfalutin cocktail of traditional Elizabethan theater and balls-to-the-wall drunken shenanigans. Accept no poor relations, pale imitations or paltry recreations, see the authentic Shit-faced Shakespeare® show which started it all. Featuring a revolving cast of Boston’s finest actors, the choicest cuts of Shakespearian classics and more inebriated antics than you can violently shake a cod piece at. Shit-faced Shakespeare® is the unique theatrical experience that has left audiences roaring in the aisles the world over. title: MAIN STAGE: Pedja Mužijević, piano | From Shadow to Spotlight
description: All the composers on this hour-long program were marginalized one way or another in their lifetime. Clara Schumann was a celebrated piano virtuoso, but she composed in an era when composition was considered a man’s job. Franz Schubert was only beginning to receive the public recognition when he died at the age of 31. George Antheil, John Cage, and Erik Satie each marched to their own beat, and the musical establishment made fun of them for it. Fortunately, all five left behind a treasure trove of works that lets us celebrate their rich artistic legacies today. Pianist Pedja Muzijevic weaves music and words into a program that crosses borders and styles and brings these overlooked artists and their stories back to life. Chapter 1 C. Schumann: Le Ballet des Revenents, op. 5 no. 4 G. Antheil: Selections from La femme 100 têtes C. Schumann: Romance, op. 5 no. 3 G. Antheil: Selections from La femme 100 têtes C. Schumann: Caprice à la Boléro, op. 5 no. 2 Chapter 2 E. Satie: Fifth Gnossienne (1889) E. Satie: Excerpts from A Mammal’s Notebook (1895-1924)J. Cage: Music for Piano 4-19 (1960) J. Cage: Excerpts from Communication (1958) E. Satie: The Three Distinguished Waltzes of a Jaded Dandy (1914) J. Cage: Excerpt from Lecture on Something (1958) J. Cage: A Room (1943) Chapter 3 F. Schubert: Sonata in A minor, D. 845 (1825) Main Stage Series Main Stage events are where the magic happens. Experience performances that inspire, challenge, and resonate long after the final note. You’ll hear bold artistic ideas and exceptional musicianship, often featuring Longy’s distinguished faculty-artists and innovative artistic partners. Each event offers a rare opportunity to be part of artistry that is both inspirational in the moment and lasting in its impact. Longy’s performances are free and open to the public, but please register in advance. title: Boston Celtic Music Festival 2027
description: Boston Celtic Music Festival 2027 The 24th annual Boston Celtic Music Festival presented by Passim, known as BCMFest, returns to Club Passim, Somerville Theatre, Crystal Ballroom, Arts at the Armory, and The Rockwell January 14-17, 2027. Presented by Passim, a Cambridge-based non-profit that supports a vibrant music community through Club Passim, the Passim School of Music, artist grants and outreach initiatives. The 2027 festival will showcase Greater Boston ’s deep tradition of music, song and dance from Irish , Scottish, Cape Breton, Quebecois and other Celtic communities. BCMFest features acts that are traditional as well as others that draw on contemporary sounds and ideas; full-time, professional touring acts as well as local session musicians; highlighting performers from across the generations. Saturday’s Dayfest offers over six hours of entertainment, from mid-morning until 6 pm. Artists will be presenting all manner of Celtic music, from classic traditional to contemporary sounds. All events will take place in Davis Sq. in Somerville at The Crystal Ballroom, The Rockwell, and Dragon’s Lair Pizza (for our sessions). Chase began teaching at Berklee in 1981 and served as chair of Ear Training there (2008-21). title: Joe Hunt Group
description: $15 admission / Start 8:30pm / Doors 8pm / Seated Show Modern jazz played by Boston's best jazz musicians. Joe Hunt is a jazz drummer, educator, author, and historian. In the early 1960s, Joe Hunt performed and recorded alongside the late NEC Distinguished Artist-in-Residence Emeritus George Russell, with releases on Decca and Riverside. Hunt joined The Stan Getz Quartet in 1964, recording several releases on Verve, then was a member of the Bill Evans Trio from 1966-1967. The remainder of the 1960s found Hunt performing or recording with several other jazz luminaries including Chet Baker, Eric Dolphy, Dizzy Gillespie, Dexter Gordon, Charles Mingus, Bob Brookmeyer, and the late Herb Pomeroy. In the 1970s and 1980s, Hunt was a member of The National Jazz Ensemble, led jazz groups with John Scofield, Mike Stern, and Santi Debriano, and toured with quartets of Red Rodney and Hal McKusick. The 1990s, and beyond, have included membership in The Smithsonian Jazz Masters Orchestra, with former NEC president Gunther Schuller, performances with Kenny Burrell, Joe Lavano, Joanne Brackeen, and Tal Farlow, as well as recordings with the Bert Seager Quintet, and also, Trio. Hunt is the author of the 1994 book 52nd Street Beat, which is a historical look at jazz drummer greats from 1945 to 1965. The Joe Hunt quartet features a modern jazz ensemble music played by top local pros: Mark Pinto - alto saxophone, formerly years with the Buddy Rich band John Lockwood – bass, formerly with Joe Henderson, Lee Konitz, current Fringe member Yuka Hamano Hunt – piano, voice, arranger Joe Hunt – drums, formerly with George Russell, Stan Getz, Jim Hall, Dexter Gordon, and Bill Evans We pay tribute to a special composer or performer at most performances. Recent shows have included: Burt Bacharach, Ahmad Jamal, Bill Evans, and Gigi Gryce. Future shows will include the music of Paul and Carla Bley, and arranger, Johnny Mandel. - Continuing of the 3rd Sunday of Every Month

title: Physical Comedy Technique: Acting & Clowning Shake Hands
description: 8 Week Clown Class with Sheriden Thomas What makes a good clown can make a better actor—and what makes a good actor can make a better clown. Come play with the tools that make comedy work. We’ll put timing, progression, dynamics, status, and physical storytelling center stage, along with a playful glossary of techniques and sayings gathered over decades of studying, performing, directing, and teaching acting and physical theatre. The goal is not simply to understand why something is funny, but to discover how to make it happen—and happen again. We’ll work with a shared vocabulary for recognizing, creating, sharpening, and repeating comedy onstage. Come play. Come discover what your silly self already knows about being funny. The series will culminate in a showing of the work. INSTRUCTOR BIO: Over several decades, Sheriden has acted under Actor’s Equity Contracts in the nation’s regional theatres. Starting in the 70’s, playing ingénues for the Guthrie Theatre in Minneapolis to Boston’s Moonbox Productions, garnering a Boston Critics Award for Kimberly in Kimberly Akimbo . Recently, in film, she played two Grandmas. One in Tiffany Paulson’s About Fate and another in Eric Aronson’s Any Day Now . (Now available on Prime) Sheriden has directed and taught acting at Cornell and Southern Methodist Universities. Since arriving in Boston, she directed plays and readings for Another Country, Queer Soup Productions, and Boston Playwrights’ Theatre. As Senior Lecturer Emerita, at Tufts University, she taught a variety of acting courses including Advanced Acting Lab, Shakespeare, Mask, and Physical Comedy. She directed a dozen plays, concluding with an edited video of Jeffrey Hatcher’s delightfully, silly adaptation of The Government Inspector . description: EVENT START-END TIME | 7:00 pm - 9:00 pm ET CHECK-IN BEGINS | 6:45 pm ET (Guests who are not in line to check in by 7:10 pm cannot be accommodated) WHERE | Trident Books, 338 Newbury St, Boston, MA 02115 ( map ) AGE RANGE | 30-45: This event is centered on people ages 30-45, but we welcome guests a year or two outside of that range who would feel comfortable dating people in the above age group. For ASL and any other accommodations not listed, please see more info here . About This Event Hear from real attendees in the videos at the bottom of the page! Want to get off your dating apps and meet someone in real life, but where you don’t have to find out that every cute person at the party is unavailable? Do you think that IRL speed dating is generally awkward and weird? So do we. That’s why we’re putting a Skip the Small Talk twist on dating. Skip the Small Talks are usually **NOT** for dating, but so many of y’all asked us for a dating event that we decided to make an exception! We'll be offering "big talk" conversation prompts to get you started, and we'll have lots of structure to make sure that you actually talk to people and that it's not awkward. Not feeling like answering a particular question? No worries, we'll have plenty to choose from, like, "When are you the happiest?" and, "If you were going to become close friends with me, what would I need to know about you?"

description: 8 Week Clown Class with Sheriden Thomas What makes a good clown can make a better actor—and what makes a good actor can make a better clown. We’ll put timing, progression, dynamics, status, and physical storytelling center stage, along with a playful glossary of techniques and sayings gathered over decades of studying, performing, directing, and teaching acting and physical theatre. The goal is not simply to understand why something is funny, but to discover how to make it happen—and happen again. We’ll work with a shared vocabulary for recognizing, creating, sharpening, and repeating comedy onstage. Come play. Come discover what your silly self already knows about being funny. The series will culminate in a showing of the work. INSTRUCTOR BIO: Over several decades, Sheriden has acted under Actor’s Equity Contracts in the nation’s regional theatres. Starting in the 70’s, playing ingénues for the Guthrie Theatre in Minneapolis to Boston’s Moonbox Productions, garnering a Boston Critics Award for Kimberly in Kimberly Akimbo . Recently, in film, she played two Grandmas. One in Tiffany Paulson’s About Fate and another in Eric Aronson’s Any Day Now . (Now available on Prime) Sheriden has directed and taught acting at Cornell and Southern Methodist Universities. Since arriving in Boston, she directed plays and readings for Another Country, Queer Soup Productions, and Boston Playwrights’ Theatre. As Senior Lecturer Emerita, at Tufts University, she taught a variety of acting courses including Advanced Acting Lab, Shakespeare, Mask, and Physical Comedy. She directed a dozen plays, concluding with an edited video of Jeffrey Hatcher’s delightfully, silly adaptation of The Government Inspector . title: Art + Science: Canvas
description: Have you ever wondered what happens in our conservation labs? Join members of our Straus Center staff for an informal monthly conversation about their work treating objects in our collections. Taking place just outside the Straus Center in the Lightbox Gallery, this presentation will give you the chance to get up close and hands-on with a selection of tools and materials used by conservation staff. In this session, associate paintings conservator Ellen Davis will talk about how artists have used canvas through the ages and how conservators care for the material. The Straus Center for Conservation and Technical Studies is a world leader in fine arts conservation, research, and training. The center’s laboratories are where conservation, conservation science, and curatorial practice intersect, coming together to enrich the understanding of and care for the approximately 250,000 objects in the Harvard Art Museums collections.

title: One Another Screening + Skip the Small Talk at Trident Books
description: Ever watched a movie that made you want to have a long conversation afterward? We’re making a whole night of that. Join us at Trident Books for a screening of One Another, followed by a Skip the Small Talk event where you’ll get to know the other nice people who showed up! One Another follows three people navigating the possible end of a close friendship at very different stages of life. A cross-country move, a mental health crisis, and a shift into empty-nesting have each brought up questions about what they need from the people closest to them. Filmed over three years, it’s a documentary about friendship, change, and what it means to care for each other. Then, we’ll get to meet each other! We’ll pair you up with other guests and have you switch partners every so often (kinda like speed-dating, but without the speed and without the dating). We’ll have a fabulous host leading the whole shebang, and we’ll give you question cards to guide conversation just a few notches deeper than you’d usually go so you don’t accidentally talk about what you do for work six times in a row. No film-analysis skills required, and there will absolutely not be a quiz. You don’t need to have anything insightful prepared, either. We’ll give you plenty to talk about, and you can share as much or as little as you’d like. If you don’t vibe with a question for any reason, you can always pick another one! Feel free to come alone (most people do—we promise we won’t make it weird for you) or bring a friend. We’d love to have you join us for a movie and some conversations with people you might otherwise have walked right past in the bookstore. Watch the One Another trailer here . There will be food and drinks for sale! Skip the Small Talk is dedicated to providing an inclusive, welcoming environment for everyone. description: Sh!t-Faced Shakespeare: Romeo & Juliet “Call me but love, and I’ll be new baptized.” There is no love lost between the Capulet and Montague families and everyone in Verona knows it. Shit-faced Shakespeare® has delighted audiences all over the States with their highfalutin cocktail of traditional Elizabethan theater and balls-to-the-wall drunken shenanigans. Accept no poor relations, pale imitations or paltry recreations, see the authentic Shit-faced Shakespeare® show which started it all. Featuring a revolving cast of Boston’s finest actors, the choicest cuts of Shakespearian classics and more inebriated antics than you can violently shake a cod piece at. Shit-faced Shakespeare® is the unique theatrical experience that has left audiences roaring in the aisles the world over. title: Barabas - Orbit | Album Launch Concert
description: $22 admission / 7:15 doors / 7:30 show / seated & standing Orbit is the new solo album by Hungarian trumpeter, pianist, and composer Lőrinc Barabás , who now performs his solo project under the name Barabas . The album is a cinematic and meditative musical journey where neoclassical piano, ambient soundscapes, and electronic textures come together. The ten compositions explore the ideas of movement and cycles. As the world around us moves ever faster, the music invites listeners to slow down, turn inward, and discover moments of stillness. Trumpet, piano, and synthesizers engage in a musical dialogue, creating a sound world that is both intimate and expansive, moving between ambient, neoclassical, and electronic music. Throughout his nearly two-decade career, Lőrinc Barabás has released thirteen albums , performed regularly across Europe and the United States, and collaborated with artists including Erik Truffaz, Takuya Kuroda, Niklas Paschburg, and Valerie June . His international appearances include the EFG London Jazz Festival at the Barbican , the Jazzycolors Festival in Paris , The Town Hall in New York City , Expo 2020 Dubai , and Expo 2025 Osaka . The album launch concert at The Lilypad in Cambridge, just outside Boston , brings the world of Orbit to life on stage, where acoustic instruments and electronics merge into one continuous, immersive musical experience.

title: Arts at the Armory Spotlight Series Presents Boston Dance Theater
description: Boston Dance Theater presents their original contemporary piece, "Unfurling," an original, nature-inspired dance performance to the Spotlight Series stage. Unfurling is a site-responsive performance created by the artists of Boston Dance Theater in collaboration with visual artist Kim Radochia. Drawing inspiration from the quiet resilience of plant life and the writings of Indigenous botanist Robin Wall Kimmerer, the work invites audiences into a shared sensory experience of movement, sound, and sculptural installation. Dancers move through the space like tendrils of growth, attuning to one another, the land, and the invisible networks that sustain life. Rooted in slowness, sensitivity, and ecological imagination, Unfurling asks us to notice what is often overlooked and to sense our place within a living, interdependent world. Tickets available now for Boston Dance Theater’s Unfurling! Doors will open at 5:00pm on Jan 31. The dance performance will begin at 6:00pm. The audience is invited to stay after for a brief post-show talkback with Boston Dance Theater's company members. Tickets: $35 for General Admission seating. Questions? Contact Arts at the Armory at 617-718-2191 or info@artsatthearmory.org Prior to the evening performance of Unfurling, Boston Dance Theater will lead a free movement workshop at 1:00pm in the Mezzanine area of the Performance Hall. title: Physical Comedy Technique: Acting & Clowning Shake Hands
description: 8 Week Clown Class with Sheriden Thomas What makes a good clown can make a better actor—and what makes a good actor can make a better clown. Come play with the tools that make comedy work. We’ll put timing, progression, dynamics, status, and physical storytelling center stage, along with a playful glossary of techniques and sayings gathered over decades of studying, performing, directing, and teaching acting and physical theatre. The goal is not simply to understand why something is funny, but to discover how to make it happen—and happen again. We’ll work with a shared vocabulary for recognizing, creating, sharpening, and repeating comedy onstage. Come play. Come discover what your silly self already knows about being funny. The series will culminate in a showing of the work. INSTRUCTOR BIO: Over several decades, Sheriden has acted under Actor’s Equity Contracts in the nation’s regional theatres. Starting in the 70’s, playing ingénues for the Guthrie Theatre in Minneapolis to Boston’s Moonbox Productions, garnering a Boston Critics Award for Kimberly in Kimberly Akimbo . Recently, in film, she played two Grandmas. One in Tiffany Paulson’s About Fate and another in Eric Aronson’s Any Day Now . (Now available on Prime) Sheriden has directed and taught acting at Cornell and Southern Methodist Universities. Since arriving in Boston, she directed plays and readings for Another Country, Queer Soup Productions, and Boston Playwrights’ Theatre. As Senior Lecturer Emerita, at Tufts University, she taught a variety of acting courses including Advanced Acting Lab, Shakespeare, Mask, and Physical Comedy. She directed a dozen plays, concluding with an edited video of Jeffrey Hatcher’s delightfully, silly adaptation of The Government Inspector . description: Charles McBee: “You Had To Be There” SHOW DESCRIPTION: Step into the good old days and laugh your way through them. Comedian Charles McBee takes the stage for a full hour of sharp, warm, and wildly funny stand-up about love, life, and everything that made the 1900s… well, the 1900s. Audiences can’t stop raving, and it’s easy to see why. Charles brings the same razor-sharp wit that earned him a Writers Guild Award nomination and credits on the MTV Video Music Awards, the Golden Globes, and beyond. His knack for finding the comedy in then-versus-now has built him a devoted social media following — and now he’s bringing it all live. Come for the laughs. Stay for the memories. You really had to be there. ARTIST BIO: Charles McBee is a NYC stand-up comedian, writer, and unapologetic 80s/’90s baby from Toledo, Ohio. He’s made three national appearances on Gotham Comedy Live, was a standout on FOX’s Laughs and Punchline (Seasons 1 & 2), and has written for everything from VH1’s Hip Hop Honors to the 2020 VMAs and the 2021 Golden Globes. He most recently served as Head Writer for Comedy Central’s Hell of a Week with Charlamagne Tha God, earning a Writers Guild Award nomination, and was a creative consultant on Nick Cannon’s Wild’ N Out. Charles has also built a dedicated social media following with his hilarious takes on pop culture, relationships, and the beautiful chaos of growing up in the analog era. If you’ve ever eaten a microwave dinner on a folding tray table, feared getting caught in a game of freeze tag, or lived through dial-up internet, Charles has a joke for you. Come see why his fans keep coming back. ARTIST SOCIALS: @charlesmcbee Timeline: DOORS: 6:15 PM SHOW: 7:00 PM Age Limit: This event is All Ages. ID: Valid ID required for alcohol consumption. title: Sh!t-Faced Shakespeare: Romeo & Juliet
description: Sh!t-Faced Shakespeare: Romeo & Juliet “Call me but love, and I’ll be new baptized.” There is no love lost between the Capulet and Montague families and everyone in Verona knows it. Certainly the only way to mend centuries of bad blood is by having two forlorn teenagers from opposite households fall in love with each other, right? Nothing that a swig (or two) of the finest spirits can’t fix! Featuring Shakespeare’s most famous feuding family, cousins without a cause, and so many faux deaths it makes daytime TV look good. Content Curious? Our shows feature murder, treason, war, violence (personal, sexual, and national), suicide, regicide, incest, and blasphemy- and that is just the Shakespeare! Our drinker has been known to contribute profanity, and the occasional bare butt-cheek. If any of this puts you off, maybe another show is more your speed. *Warning: But also, we do have sword fights, loud sounds, and flashing lights if those affect your person.* About Shit-faced Shakespeare®: An entirely serious Shakespeare play, with an entirely shit-faced cast member. The original, award winning, international smash-hit direct from London’s West End to an American theater near you! Founded in 2010 in the UK and first arriving on US shores back in 2015. Shit-faced Shakespeare® has delighted audiences all over the States with their highfalutin cocktail of traditional Elizabethan theater and balls-to-the-wall drunken shenanigans. Accept no poor relations, pale imitations or paltry recreations, see the authentic Shit-faced Shakespeare® show which started it all. Featuring a revolving cast of Boston’s finest actors, the choicest cuts of Shakespearian classics and more inebriated antics than you can violently shake a cod piece at. Shit-faced Shakespeare® is the unique theatrical experience that has left audiences roaring in the aisles the world over. description: 18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum. Ophira Eisenberg is a stand-up Comedian, Writer, and Podcast Host (NPR, CBS, The Moth, HBO, Comedy Central, iHeart) who headlines theaters and comedy venues across the world, tours regularly with the Moth Mainstage, and hosts the weekly parenting-comedy podcast Parenting is a Joke (Webby Finalist for Best Host). title: Physical Comedy Technique: Acting & Clowning Shake Hands
description: 8 Week Clown Class with Sheriden Thomas What makes a good clown can make a better actor—and what makes a good actor can make a better clown. Come play with the tools that make comedy work. We’ll put timing, progression, dynamics, status, and physical storytelling center stage, along with a playful glossary of techniques and sayings gathered over decades of studying, performing, directing, and teaching acting and physical theatre. The goal is not simply to understand why something is funny, but to discover how to make it happen—and happen again. We’ll work with a shared vocabulary for recognizing, creating, sharpening, and repeating comedy onstage. Come play. Come discover what your silly self already knows about being funny. The series will culminate in a showing of the work. INSTRUCTOR BIO: Over several decades, Sheriden has acted under Actor’s Equity Contracts in the nation’s regional theatres. Starting in the 70’s, playing ingénues for the Guthrie Theatre in Minneapolis to Boston’s Moonbox Productions, garnering a Boston Critics Award for Kimberly in Kimberly Akimbo . Recently, in film, she played two Grandmas. One in Tiffany Paulson’s About Fate and another in Eric Aronson’s Any Day Now . (Now available on Prime) Sheriden has directed and taught acting at Cornell and Southern Methodist Universities. Since arriving in Boston, she directed plays and readings for Another Country, Queer Soup Productions, and Boston Playwrights’ Theatre. As Senior Lecturer Emerita, at Tufts University, she taught a variety of acting courses including Advanced Acting Lab, Shakespeare, Mask, and Physical Comedy. She directed a dozen plays, concluding with an edited video of Jeffrey Hatcher’s delightfully, silly adaptation of The Government Inspector . title: Arts at the Armory Spotlight Series Presents Blind Boys of Alabama
description: 6x Grammy Winners return to Somerville, celebrating Stevie Wonder’s “Songs in the Key of Life” Arts at the Armory is thrilled to welcome back gospel legends Blind Boys of Alabama to the Spotlight Series on Friday, February 12, 2027. This special presentation pairs many of Stevie Wonder’s classic songs with beloved selections from the Blind Boys’ own celebrated repertoire, blending gospel, soul, and Americana in a joyful performance that honors both musical legacies. With over 75 years of lifting spirits and moving souls, the Blind Boys continue their mission of spreading light and love through the universal language of music. In 2003, the Blind Boys earned a Grammy Award for an album that included their acclaimed cover of Stevie Wonder’s “Higher Ground,” a version later featured in film and television, including FX’s Fargo. In 2007, Stevie Wonder presented Blind Boys singer Jimmy Carter with a Vision Award for Lifetime Achievement, underscoring their enduring impact on music and culture. Featuring classics like: “Sir Duke,” “I Wish,” “As,” and more. The Blind Boys of Alabama are recognized worldwide as living legends of gospel music. Celebrated by The National Endowment for the Arts (NEA) and The Recording Academy/GRAMMYs with Lifetime Achievement Awards, inducted into the Gospel Music Hall of Fame, and winners of six GRAMMY® Awards, they have attained the highest levels of achievement in a career that spans over 70 years. They have appeared on recordings with many artists, including Lou Reed, Peter Gabriel, Bonnie Raitt, Willie Nelson, Aaron Neville, Susan Tedeschi, Ben Harper, Patty Griffin, and Taj Mahal. Arts at the Armory serves delicious locally sourced food and drink at the Performance Hall bar when doors open (usually one hour before the show). Please arrive early to enjoy dinner and drinks before the event. The full menu can be viewed HERE. Check out Parking/Directions and FAQs for more information about our venue.

title: Sh!t-Faced Shakespeare: Romeo & Juliet
description: Sh!t-Faced Shakespeare: Romeo & Juliet “Call me but love, and I’ll be new baptized.” There is no love lost between the Capulet and Montague families and everyone in Verona knows it. Certainly the only way to mend centuries of bad blood is by having two forlorn teenagers from opposite households fall in love with each other, right? Nothing that a swig (or two) of the finest spirits can’t fix! Featuring Shakespeare’s most famous feuding family, cousins without a cause, and so many faux deaths it makes daytime TV look good. Content Curious? Our shows feature murder, treason, war, violence (personal, sexual, and national), suicide, regicide, incest, and blasphemy- and that is just the Shakespeare! Our drinker has been known to contribute profanity, and the occasional bare butt-cheek. If any of this puts you off, maybe another show is more your speed. *Warning: But also, we do have sword fights, loud sounds, and flashing lights if those affect your person.* About Shit-faced Shakespeare®: An entirely serious Shakespeare play, with an entirely shit-faced cast member. The original, award winning, international smash-hit direct from London’s West End to an American theater near you! Founded in 2010 in the UK and first arriving on US shores back in 2015. Shit-faced Shakespeare® has delighted audiences all over the States with their highfalutin cocktail of traditional Elizabethan theater and balls-to-the-wall drunken shenanigans. Accept no poor relations, pale imitations or paltry recreations, see the authentic Shit-faced Shakespeare® show which started it all. Featuring a revolving cast of Boston’s finest actors, the choicest cuts of Shakespearian classics and more inebriated antics than you can violently shake a cod piece at. Shit-faced Shakespeare® is the unique theatrical experience that has left audiences roaring in the aisles the world over. description: EVENT START-END TIME | 7:00 pm - 9:00 pm ET CHECK-IN BEGINS | 6:45 pm ET (Guests who are not in line to check in by 7:10 pm cannot be accommodated) WHERE | Trident Books, 338 Newbury St, Boston, MA 02115 ( map ) AGE RANGE | 30-45: This event is centered on people ages 30-45, but we welcome guests a year or two outside of that range who would feel comfortable dating people in the above age group. If you are outside of this age range, don't worry-- we have a lot of other events on our calendar, including all-ages events, that might be a better fit! FOOD/DRINKS | The entire Trident menu of food and alcoholic as well as nonalcoholic drinks will be available for purchase, with many allergy-friendly options for food and drinks. PARKING / PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION | Limited parking lot spots and street parking may be available nearby, but public transportation is recommended. ACCESSIBILITY & OTHER VENUE DETAILS | Wheelchair accessible, gender-neutral bathrooms available, noise isolation devices used. For ASL and any other accommodations not listed, please see more info here . About This Event Hear from real attendees in the videos at the bottom of the page! Want to get off your dating apps and meet someone in real life, but where you don’t have to find out that every cute person at the party is unavailable? Do you think that IRL speed dating is generally awkward and weird? So do we. That’s why we’re putting a Skip the Small Talk twist on dating. Skip the Small Talks are usually **NOT** for dating, but so many of y’all asked us for a dating event that we decided to make an exception! We'll be offering "big talk" conversation prompts to get you started, and we'll have lots of structure to make sure that you actually talk to people and that it's not awkward. Not feeling like answering a particular question? No worries, we'll have plenty to choose from, like, "When are you the happiest?" and, "If you were going to become close friends with me, what would I need to know about you?"

title: Sh!t-Faced Shakespeare: Romeo & Juliet
description: Sh!t-Faced Shakespeare: Romeo & Juliet “Call me but love, and I’ll be new baptized.” There is no love lost between the Capulet and Montague families and everyone in Verona knows it. Certainly the only way to mend centuries of bad blood is by having two forlorn teenagers from opposite households fall in love with each other, right? Nothing that a swig (or two) of the finest spirits can’t fix! Featuring Shakespeare’s most famous feuding family, cousins without a cause, and so many faux deaths it makes daytime TV look good. Content Curious? Our shows feature murder, treason, war, violence (personal, sexual, and national), suicide, regicide, incest, and blasphemy- and that is just the Shakespeare! Our drinker has been known to contribute profanity, and the occasional bare butt-cheek. If any of this puts you off, maybe another show is more your speed. *Warning: But also, we do have sword fights, loud sounds, and flashing lights if those affect your person.* About Shit-faced Shakespeare®: An entirely serious Shakespeare play, with an entirely shit-faced cast member. The original, award winning, international smash-hit direct from London’s West End to an American theater near you! Founded in 2010 in the UK and first arriving on US shores back in 2015. Shit-faced Shakespeare® has delighted audiences all over the States with their highfalutin cocktail of traditional Elizabethan theater and balls-to-the-wall drunken shenanigans. Accept no poor relations, pale imitations or paltry recreations, see the authentic Shit-faced Shakespeare® show which started it all. Featuring a revolving cast of Boston’s finest actors, the choicest cuts of Shakespearian classics and more inebriated antics than you can violently shake a cod piece at. Shit-faced Shakespeare® is the unique theatrical experience that has left audiences roaring in the aisles the world over. SOCIAL MEDIA: www.shit-facedshakespeare.us Timeline: DOORS: 6:15 PM SHOW: 7:00 PM RUNTIME: 1 hour 15 minutes Age Limit: This event

title: MAIN STAGE | Niloufar Nourbakhsh in collaboration with Ensemble Decipher | Tactile Transmissions | Faculty Artist Recital
description: Stones wired with motion sensors. Vintage radios feeding back into acoustic instruments. Cassette tape that has been physically mangled and put back in the machine. Ensemble Decipher builds instruments out of things that were never meant to be instruments, then plays them. Every work on this program is about transmission and what gets warped along the way. Rhizome Music sends live drums through microphones into vintage radios and back into the acoustic instruments, building a hall of mirrors out of sound. Stone Dreams attaches motion sensors to stones and transmits the data by radio, turning the stones themselves into the instrument. Of Breath and Feeding Back takes up aging and the loss of youth. Marti Epstein’s new work pairs toy pianos with cassette players loaded with altered tape, producing what she calls a nostalgic soundworld. Erin Rogers’ Telegraph runs from homing pigeons to electrical telegraphy, with nonsense text passed between players while one performer mixes the room live. Plus works by ensemble members Nourbakhsh, Bohigian, and Cosgrove. Sit close. Main Stage Series Main Stage events are where the magic happens. Experience performances that inspire, challenge, and resonate long after the final note. You’ll hear bold artistic ideas and exceptional musicianship, often featuring Longy’s distinguished faculty-artists and innovative artistic partners. Each event offers a rare opportunity to be part of artistry that is both inspirational in the moment and lasting in its impact. Longy’s performance are free and open to the public, but please register in advance.

title: MAIN STAGE | Collage New Music | Doubles
description: Two voices meeting, colliding, connecting. Doubles moves through spatialized instrumental pairings, opposing musical gestures, and works drawn from childhood objects, online communication, and social change. Dialogue arrives as cooperation, tension, echo, and interruption. Blues, bluegrass, and contemporary classical influences run through the instrumental and vocal duos, with student performers joining in. The program closes with two sextets for full ensemble, widening the conversation from intimate exchange to shared musical space. Main Stage Series Main Stage events are where the magic happens. Experience performances that inspire, challenge, and resonate long after the final note. You’ll hear bold artistic ideas and exceptional musicianship, often featuring Longy’s distinguished faculty-artists and innovative artistic partners. Each event offers a rare opportunity to be part of artistry that is both inspirational in the moment and lasting in its impact.

title: Physical Comedy Technique: Acting & Clowning Shake Hands
description: 8 Week Clown Class with Sheriden Thomas What makes a good clown can make a better actor—and what makes a good actor can make a better clown. Come play with the tools that make comedy work. We’ll put timing, progression, dynamics, status, and physical storytelling center stage, along with a playful glossary of techniques and sayings gathered over decades of studying, performing, directing, and teaching acting and physical theatre. The goal is not simply to understand why something is funny, but to discover how to make it happen—and happen again. We’ll work with a shared vocabulary for recognizing, creating, sharpening, and repeating comedy onstage. Come play. Come discover what your silly self already knows about being funny. The series will culminate in a showing of the work. INSTRUCTOR BIO: Over several decades, Sheriden has acted under Actor’s Equity Contracts in the nation’s regional theatres. Starting in the 70’s, playing ingénues for the Guthrie Theatre in Minneapolis to Boston’s Moonbox Productions, garnering a Boston Critics Award for Kimberly in Kimberly Akimbo . Recently, in film, she played two Grandmas. One in Tiffany Paulson’s About Fate and another in Eric Aronson’s Any Day Now . (Now available on Prime) Sheriden has directed and taught acting at Cornell and Southern Methodist Universities. Since arriving in Boston, she directed plays and readings for Another Country, Queer Soup Productions, and Boston Playwrights’ Theatre. As Senior Lecturer Emerita, at Tufts University, she taught a variety of acting courses including Advanced Acting Lab, Shakespeare, Mask, and Physical Comedy. She directed a dozen plays, concluding with an edited video of Jeffrey Hatcher’s delightfully, silly adaptation of The Government Inspector .
